paper_title: Probing the Blue Axion with Cosmic Optical Background Anisotropies
suggested_experiment_name: HST COB anisotropy 606 nm (blue axion, CDM)
coupling_convention: decay rate Gamma_{a->gamma gamma} in s^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 8 (CDM panel); NOT converted to g_agamma (conversion Gamma = g^2 m_a^3 / 64 pi would be applied downstream)
notes: Paper recomputes the HST 606 nm COB anisotropy bound on decaying axion-like dark matter ('blue axion', ma ~ 5-25 eV) with improved analysis, and forecasts 438/336 nm sensitivities. Main exclusion results are lifetime/decay-rate curves (Gamma_a->gg vs m_a) shown only in figures (Figs. 1, 6, 8, 9) and are not tabulated. The only explicit numerical limit in the text is from the Note Added: for ma = 4.2 eV (MUSE filter gap), Gamma >= 3.03e-25 s^-1 is excluded, corresponding to g_agamma >= 2.33e-11 GeV^-1 — emitted as the single data point. The full 5-25 eV exclusion curve (rising from ~few x 1e-26 s^-1 in rate) could not be reliably digitized from text alone. Cosmological (not local) DM density assumed (Omega_CDM h^2 = 0.12), so dm_density_assumed is null. Bound applies equally to g_agamma (a->2gamma) and g_agammachi (dark portal a->chi+gamma).
